q_en:
Comprehension:
Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

Surveillance has increased manifold since the 9/11 terror attacks on the World Trade Centre in the U.S. This increase in surveillance today shapes the relationship between the state and the individual. The state keeps an eye on its citizens, thereby positing each and every citizen as a potential wrong-doer. For instance, the proliferation of CCTV cameras in streets, restaurants and in every imaginable public space. In fact, the camera need not even be functional in order to make the citizens behave themselves – its mere presence is enough to scare the citizens into submission. Such is the power of the mere potential of surveillance. Surveillance studies have shown that these techniques might not be too effective at all times, as citizens might feign decent behaviour to avoid themselves from involving into a tussle with the law of the land. But it does not assure the state of the reformation in the attitude of the citizens.

q_en:
Comprehension:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow.

Creating art is also a perfect way of encouraging special needs children to bond with their family members. As adults we are distracted by the endless demands on our stressful lives and, thus, many of us lose that innate ability to connect with our creative energies. Fortunately, the spark never dies out, and it only takes a simple art activity like pal painting with your child to rekindle that close bond. Creating art, looking at a work of art or even watching an artist at work helps children feel calm, joyous, and happy. As their hands move on the paper, their eyes start following the movement and slowly their breathing becomes calm and steady. Studies show that art activities help to build better hand-eye coordination, and improve concentration, and thus play an important part in art therapy as well as being an effective teaching tool for a variety of subjects.
